content: Pre-INDX, 9 full turns on the tensioning screws (alternating back and forth) starting from the pulley assemblies being flush with the tensioner housings put you right in the ballpark for correct belt tension. I went 8 turns and the belts were WAY too tight. 5–6 full turns seems to be about right for the INDX mounting plate. I followed someone else’s suggestion and set my belts in the plate so the ends were ~1mm inset from flush on the edges of the mounting plate.

Not sure what particular version is show in the pictures, but 8mm on an original Core One that has been upgraded several times would shatter the tensioners.  5.5 full turns was as far as I was willing to go, and the belt strum sounded pretty close to tight.

I would recommend that you position both tensioning mechanisms flush as shown both and then tighten the left one 1/2 turn and then tighten the right one 1/2 turn and repeat until you've done both roughly 16 half turns ( or 8 full turns ).  Then check how far each tensioner has moved.  They both should have moved about 3mm which you should be able to see ( and measure ).  That seems to be about the right tension for now.  The important part here is to switch back and forth when tightening.
I tightened my belts using these pictures as a guide. They turned out to be so tight that the belt tension wizard didn't work. It took me a while to figure out that they needed to be loosened
Belts seem insanely tight - hope this works...

replies.content: Yeah belts feel tighter than a puckered end

I didn't tighten the belts this much (pre-GT1.5 belts needed far less) and had all sorts of trouble with belt calibration.  Tightened them up and bingo, calibration is fine.

Homing calibration still took forever but did at least work.  And I now finally have all four docks calibrated.  It only took half a day....
